newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to move towards 4,680 then slip back.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to move towards 4,680 then slip back.

text.p: Stock market bears will be unable to capitalise too much on the weak state of the London stock market on Thursday, technical analysts said.
The FTSE 100 index began to pick itself up off the floor at 4,628 on Wednesday and may continue its tentative recovery aiming to reach the region near 4,680 before slipping back, they added.
Although medium-term downward pressure still exists investor anxiety may have begun to ease and this will allow a few bargain hunters to chance their luck on a few hard-hit stocks.
By 0712 GMT, the FTSE was indicated unchanged at 4,657.0.
By dipping down to 4,628 on Wednesday, the FTSE had made a normal two-thirds retracement target of the rally to 4,796 -- its intra-day high of June 13 -- from the low of 4,535 on June 5.
There now exists a chance for the index to make a small revival before having another relapse, analysts said.
The index is currently locked in by a pair of downwardly sloping trendlines which connect its intra-day highs and lows over the past four days.
These lines are falling at an average of 36 points a day but the vertical distance between the lines indicate that increased turbulence could mean a 90 point daily range is possible.
Based on a trendline analysis on a tick chart of the FTSE, the index should encounter resistance from the 4,670-4,680 region and could then backtrack towards 4,630.
